Definition: from G4579; a commotion, i.e. (of the air) a gale, (of the ground) an earthquake:--earthquake, tempest.
BiblicalUsage: A seismos is an earthquake, a shaking of the ground, and it opens prisons and ends ages. At Philippi there was suddenly a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken, and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed. And Jesus warned that great earthquakes shall be in divers places, with famines and pestilences, before the end.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the earthquake at Philippi is the pattern: God shakes the foundations, the doors open, and the bands fall off.
